items.followUp: What is the role of the cell plate during cytokinesis in plant cells?

rubric.why: Identifies the phragmoplast as a microtubule structure formed between the daughter nuclei.
rubric.description: Names the phragmoplast as a microtubule structure associated with the dividing plant cell.
rubric.how: Award for identifying its microtubule structure or its position between the daughter nuclei.

rubric.why: States the phragmoplast’s role in cell-plate formation and separation of the daughter cells.
rubric.description: Explains that it guides cell-plate formation, leading to a new wall that separates the daughter cells.
rubric.how: Award for linking cell-plate or new-wall formation to separation of the daughter cells.

modelAnswer: The phragmoplast is a structure of microtubules that forms between the two daughter nuclei during plant-cell division.
It guides the formation of a cell plate, which develops into a new cell wall and separates the daughter cells.

items.followUp: What is meant by an enzyme-substrate complex?

rubric.why: Defines the active site as the substrate-binding region of an enzyme.
rubric.description: States that the active site is a specific region of an enzyme where its substrate binds.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the enzyme region and its relationship to the substrate.

rubric.why: Gives both functions: substrate binding and catalysis of the reaction.
rubric.description: States that the active site binds the substrate and catalyses its conversion into product.
rubric.how: Award when both substrate binding and catalytic action are stated.

modelAnswer: The active site is the specific region of an enzyme to which its substrate binds.
It binds the substrate and catalyses its conversion into product.

items.followUp: What is one structural difference between saturated and unsaturated fats?

rubric.why: States the defining bond feature of saturated fatty acids.
rubric.description: Saturated fatty acids have no carbon-carbon double bonds.
rubric.how: Award for stating that saturated fatty acids contain no double bonds.

rubric.why: States the defining bond feature of unsaturated fatty acids.
rubric.description: Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more carbon-carbon double bonds.
rubric.how: Award for stating that unsaturated fatty acids contain at least one double bond.

modelAnswer: Saturated fatty acids have no carbon-carbon double bonds.
Unsaturated fatty acids have one or more carbon-carbon double bonds.

items.followUp: Explain four more careers related to Biology.

rubric.why: Provides a biology-related career and explains its contribution.
rubric.description: Medicine uses biological knowledge to understand the body, diagnose disease, and treat patients.
rubric.how: Award for correctly naming medicine or a medical profession and describing its work.

rubric.why: Provides a distinct biology-related career and explains its contribution.
rubric.description: Agriculture applies biology to improve crops or livestock and increase food production.
rubric.how: Award for correctly naming agriculture and describing its application.

rubric.why: Provides a distinct biology-related career and explains its contribution.
rubric.description: Fisheries applies biology to fish breeding, rearing, or management of fish resources.
rubric.how: Award for correctly naming fisheries or aquaculture and describing its work.

rubric.why: Provides a distinct biology-related career and explains its contribution.
rubric.description: Forestry applies biological knowledge to manage and conserve forests and their resources.
rubric.how: Award for correctly naming forestry or foresters and describing forest management or conservation.

modelAnswer: Medicine: Medical professionals use biology to understand the human body, diagnose diseases, and treat patients.
Agriculture: Agricultural scientists use biology to improve crops and livestock and increase food production.
Fisheries: Fisheries specialists use biology to breed and rear fish and manage fish resources.
Forestry: Foresters use biological knowledge to manage and conserve forests and their resources.
